chunks: Safwan ibn Suhayl narrated from Ibn Muskān, from Layth, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prayer in summer during the short nights: 'Do I pray in the first part of the night?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَوَّلِ اللَّيْلِ: The first part of the night

ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayers during the short nights of summer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Sahih al-Tusi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of praying during the short summer nights by performing them in the 'first part of the night' (awwal al-layl), a practice often associated with the flexibility of combining prayers or praying early to avoid the heat and the brevity of the night. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (taysir) in worship, allowing believers to maintain their devotional obligations without undue hardship during seasonal variations in daylight hours.
